Challenge Description: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

The Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge focuses on developing an interactive and educational training platform that introduces school students and young learners to the exciting world of space exploration and astronaut life.

The goal is to create a virtual astronaut training experience where students can learn about space science, spacecraft operations, microgravity, space missions, astronaut responsibilities

ASTROQUEST – Smart Space Outpost Simulator

ASTROQUEST is an interactive educational game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.” The project aims to help students understand the engineering challenges of establishing and maintaining a human settlement on the Moon or Mars. Players take the role of an outpost commander and manage essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and electricity while maintaining life-support systems and radiation protection. They can build and upgrade facilities, respond to unexpected emergencies, and make critical decisions that affect the survival of the crew. Each decision involves engineering trade-offs, helping players understand how different systems depend on one another. ASTROQUEST transforms space science concepts into an engaging gaming experience while encouraging problem-solving, critical thinking, resource management, and engineering skills among young learners.
details:
ASTROQUEST – Smart Space Outpost Simulator

ASTROQUEST is an interactive educational game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.” It allows students to experience the challenges of managing a human settlement on the Moon or Mars by taking the role of an outpost commander.

The game works through resource management and decision-making. Players must maintain essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and electricity while managing life-support systems, radiation protection, and food production. They can build and upgrade facilities, respond to unexpected emergencies, and make engineering decisions that directly affect the survival of the crew and the success of the mission.

The project aims to make space science more engaging and understandable for young learners. It helps develop critical thinking, problem-solving, resource management, and decision-making skills by allowing students to experience the consequences of their choices in a simulated space environment.

The planned development technology includes React.js, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS, with Antigravity as an AI-assisted development tool. The game is designed as a browser-based simulation, with a focus on an accessible and interactive user experience.

The creative aspect of ASTROQUEST is its combination of educational learning and space survival gameplay. Instead of simply presenting facts about space exploration, it allows players to experiment with different strategies and understand engineering trade-offs. Our two-member team considered educational value, gameplay simplicity, resource balance, scientific relevance, accessibility, and the importance of making the experience enjoyable for students.

Our intended impact is to inspire young learners to explore space science and engineering while helping them understand the complex decisions involved in sustaining human life beyond Earth.
